newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain gov't approves law to improve fiscal rigour.
newsitem.headline: Spain gov't approves law to improve fiscal rigour.

text.p: The Spanish cabinet has approved a bill to improve fiscal discipline and ensure no further budget "holes" appear, the Economy Ministry said on Friday.

The bill is designed to avoid a recurrence of the unwelcome summer discovery of a 721 billion peseta shortfall in the 1995 budget, inherited by the new conservative government from the previous socialist administration.
The hole represented items neither paid nor accounted for and items which had been paid but were not included in the accounts, the four month-old government has said.

The bill establishes that advances of funds agreed in one budget will be cancelled in the same year. Most directly, the bill prevents pushing obligations forward into future budgetary years, the Ministry statement said.

"With this we will correct the circumstances that gave way to the lack of budget allocation in the apropriate year and we restrict the possibility of passing over expenditures to future years," the Ministry said.
